concepts.gloss_en: the calm and pure air — the atmosphere of rest/peace (calm air) produced by love and tzedakah, in which spirits repose one in another

members.note: representative; fuller form 'calm and pure air'

same referent within lm1:17 — the calm/restful air (אויר הנח = spirits at rest, no ruach ra'ah of hatred). The longer form merely adds the descriptor והזך ('and pure'); both name the identical 'calm air' motif of love/tzedakah in this Torah

notes: Both forms occur only in lm1:17 and share the head 'אויר הנח'. Merged as one concept with the shorter form tiered 'likely' (not 'obvious') because it is a shorter phrase, not a pure orthographic variant. If the reviewer treats the added adjective והזך as introducing a distinct emphasis, they may split; under-merge risk is low here since the referent is clearly the same.
